subject: Control + Data Plane Trust Zones and Edge Relay — on-prem VPC review
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@astra-health.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: network-team@astra-health.com
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00Z
Subject: On‑prem VPC: control/data plane trust zones + edge relay — kickoff

Hi Soojin / Markus,

Thanks for putting time on this. We're starting lock‑in work for a private Redwood deployment inside Astra's production VPCs. We want a short architecture review focused on:
- clear separation between control plane (management, model orchestration) and data plane (inference nodes),
- trust zones for tenant isolation,
- an edge relay pattern for telemetry, metrics and optional public callbacks,
- egress control and auditing for PHI handling (we're HIPAA bound).

Attached are two sketches from our network team (they're rough). Can you review and call out: required firewall rules / subnet boundaries, mTLS trust anchors, cert rotation notes, and any implications for auditing and log export?

We're available for a 30‑minute review Tuesday or Wednesday.

Cheers,
Priya Shah
Lead DevOps, Astra Health
attachments: network-sketch-1.png (png), network-sketch-2.pdf (pdf)
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@astra-health.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-28T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: On‑prem VPC: control/data plane trust zones + edge relay — kickoff

Thanks Priya — quick ack and some initial comments before we schedule:

- Happy to run a 30m walkthrough. Wednesday 10/29 14:00 ET or Thursday 10/30 11:00 ET works for our infra folks.
- At a high level, Redwoods' recommended pattern is:
  * Control plane lives in a dedicated management VPC/subnet with strict inbound rules (SSH prohibited except from admin jump hosts, HTTPS/GRPC only to our control endpoints).
  * Data plane (inference workers) run in customer‑owned subnets with egress to an edge relay/proxy we can deploy into a DMZ subnet; no direct outbound to public internet from inference hosts.
  * Edge relay handles authenticated forwarding of telemetry, optional webhooks, and token exchange for limited external callbacks.
- We'll produce a reference diagram and a short egress matrix (who can talk to what, over which ports).
- Quick red flags for PHI: ensure audit logs for request/response metadata never leave in plaintext; we recommend KMS envelope encryption for logs and a separate logging sink under your control.

I'll attach a concise reference pack (diagram + runbook draft) and a table of required security groups / ACLs.

Thanks — Soojin
So‑ojin Lee (she/her)
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@astra-health.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-28T15:24:00Z
Subject: Re: On‑prem VPC: control/data plane trust zones + edge relay — kickoff

Priya — adding a few specifics from the control‑plane runtime perspective so the network team can validate: 

1) Control plane endpoints (API, orchestration, model registry) require 2‑way mTLS. We'll provide CA certs for verification; customer must allow client cert validation at the edge/proxy layer. Typical ports: 443 (TLS), 8443 (control‑plane GRPC) — we can consolidate over mutual TLS on 443 if that's preferred.

2) Data plane inference nodes open outbound to the edge relay on a single persistent TLS connection (we use a long‑lived TLS session with a keepalive). That relay is the only thing that should reach the control plane on behalf of workers — prevents lateral control plane access.

3) KV cache and model layer storage: if you plan to host model artifacts on an internal object store, ensure the control plane and edge relay can reach the storage endpoint over private routing. Avoid public S3 endpoints; prefer VPC endpoints.

4) Cert rotation: we support short‑lived node certificates minted via a provisioning service (requires outbound access to the CA endpoint during bootstrap). If bootstrap must be air‑gapped, we have an offline provisioning flow — let's call that out if needed.

I'll sketch an updated diagram and an ACL matrix for you this afternoon.

— Irene (Runtime/Serving)
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@astra-health.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: network-team@astra-health.com
Date: 2026-10-29T08:09:00Z
Subject: Re: On‑prem VPC: control/data plane trust zones + edge relay — kickoff

Thanks Irene — this is exactly the level we need. A couple quick clarifications from our network team:
- We prefer using 443 only (customer constraint: tight proxy rules). If you can fold GRPC over 443 that simplifies our ACLs.
- For telemetry: logs must be forwarded to our internal SIEM (Splunk) over an authenticated TLS channel. Can the edge relay be configured to push to an internal syslog/HTTPS collector?
- Air‑gapped bootstrap: yes, we need the offline flow explained in the runbook.

Let's go ahead and do Wednesday 14:00 ET for the walk‑through. Sending a calendar invite shortly.

— Priya
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com

Date: 2026-10-29T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: On‑prem VPC: control/data plane trust zones + edge relay — kickoff

Follow up from today's call (notes and next actions):

Notes summary:
- Consensus to terminate all control‑plane GRPC over 443 (mTLS) — Redwood will provide cert bundles and instructions for the nginx proxy at Astra gateway.
- Edge relay will be deployed into a DMZ subnet (NAT disabled for worker subnets). Workers maintain a single outbound TLS connection to relay over 443; relay performs authentication and relays traffic to control plane endpoints over an internal peering link.
- Telemetry: relay can push to an internal HTTPS collector or via syslog over TLS; we'll provide a small adapter that supports both.
- Offline provisioning: we agreed to run an offline token signing flow for initial node bootstrap; details in runbook.

Action items:
1) Redwood: share revised diagram (attached: controlplane-dataplane-trustzones-v1.png), egress matrix (edge-relay-egress-matrix.xlsx), and a draft runbook (deployment-runbook-draft.pdf). Due: 2026-10-30 EOD.
2) Astra: confirm IP ranges for DMZ and worker subnets + SIEM endpoint and any proxy interceptors.
3) Both: open JIRA INFRA-7821 for final acceptance tests (network ACL/egress validation).

We're attaching the artifacts here for your review. Please flag anything missing.

Thanks,
So‑ojin Lee
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Quick confirmation from my side — reviewed the diagram and runbook draft. Two minor items to add before we finalize:
- Note that control‑plane telemetry exports should be routed to a separate logging bucket/sink with restricted KMS key; don't mix with app logs.
- Add an explicit rollback path in the runbook for revoking node certs if we need an emergency cutover.

If Astra can confirm the DMZ CIDR and SIEM endpoint, we'll update the runbook and mark JIRA INFRA-7821 ready for your network acceptance tests.

— Markus Klein
Principal Architect, Redwood Inference
